A new report from Omdia further reveals Apple's roadmap for upcoming MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, and iPad models over the next several years. Below are the report's predictions.

The following are the new MacBook and iPad models disclosed by Omdia

Omdia has published an extensive report on the display panels that will be used in upcoming MacBook and iPad models. Based on the company's display research, it has released a roadmap of new models extending from this autumn through 2029.

The report's predictions are as follows:

Late 2026

  • MacBook Pro / Ultra: 14.3-inch and 16.3-inch OLED displays
  • iPad mini: 8.4-inch OLED display, 60Hz

Early 2027

  • MacBook Air: 13.6-inch and 15.4-inch LCD displays
  • iPad Air: 11-inch and 13-inch OLED displays, 60Hz

Mid 2027

  • iPad Pro: 11-inch and 13-inch OLED displays, adding COE technology

Late 2027

  • MacBook Pro / Ultra: 14.3-inch and 16.3-inch OLED displays, adding LTPO technology

Early 2028

2029

  • MacBook: 13.6-inch OLED display, equipped with LTPO and COE technology

Notable details in the MacBook and iPad report

There are several details worth noting in the report. For instance, the report states that after the OLED version of the MacBook Pro / Ultra launches this autumn, the mini-LED MacBook Pro models will continue to be sold until at least 2028. This may support the claim that the "Ultra" branding will be used for the OLED versions.

Secondly, the 13.6-inch MacBook slated for release in 2029 is listed as a separate new model in Omdia's timeline. However, based on earlier rumours, this model may simply be the OLED version of the MacBook Air previously reported by Bloomberg and Ming-Chi Kuo.

The MacBook Neo is notably absent from the roadmap. This may be because, as an entry-level product, no display upgrades are expected in the short term; this also explains why the report makes no mention of the basic iPad.

Finally, Omdia predicts that the OLED MacBook Pro / MacBook Ultra will offer an M5 Ultra chip option. However, this claim appears to be more speculative than substantive reporting.

What are your thoughts on the Mac and iPad roadmap? Feel free to share in the comments.
